primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome with essential hypertension and pre-diabetes

medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension in adults <55 years without contraindication

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends CCB as partner drug in ACE‑I based combination therapy

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Primary prevention of cardiovascular disease (dyslipidaemia component of metabolic syndrome)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 advise statin therapy for patients with QRISK ≥10% or ≥1 CVD risk factor

medications.dose: 500 mg once daily with evening meal, titrate to 500 mg twice daily after 1 week if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review HbA1c at 3 months then 6‑monthly
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk pre‑diabetes when lifestyle alone is insufficient

medications.dose: 120 mg three times daily with each main meal containing fat
medications.duration: Until BMI reduction of ≥5% or weight‑loss goal achieved, then review
medications.purpose: Adjunct weight‑loss therapy for obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 list orlistat as pharmacological option for obesity when lifestyle measures are inadequate

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase plasma concentrations of atorvastatin (CYP3A4 substrate), raising risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis
interactions_checked.action: Start atorvastatin at low dose (20 mg), monitor CK if muscle symptoms; consider rosuvastatin if concern persists

interactions_checked.interaction: Astemizole is metabolised by CYP3A4; higher atorvastatin levels may inhibit its clearance, increasing QT‑prolongation risk
interactions_checked.action: Switch astemizole to a non‑QT‑prolonging antihistamine (e.g., cetirizine) if possible

interactions_checked.interaction: Orlistat reduces absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins; injectable B12 is not affected but oral vitamins may be
interactions_checked.action: Separate timing of oral vitamin supplements (≥2 h before/after orlistat) and continue injectable B12 as prescribed

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² due to risk of lactic acidosis (NICE NG28)
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, consider DPP‑4 inhibitor (e.g., sitagliptin) instead

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² for metformin initiation; renal function must be checked before and after starting metformin
QRISK score not available – assumed ≥10% given hypertension, obesity, pre‑diabetes; formal QRISK calculation required to confirm statin indication
Baseline liver function tests not recorded – required before starting atorvastatin and to monitor for hepatotoxicity
Allergy status to statins, metformin, or orlistat not documented – verify before prescribing
Patient’s smoking status unknown – smoking cessation advice should be offered if applicable
treatment_summary: Continue ACE‑I (lisinopril) and up‑titrate CCB (amlodipine) to achieve target BP. Initiate atorvastatin 20 mg for primary CVD prevention, start metformin MR 500 mg daily for high‑risk pre‑diabetes, and add orlistat 120 mg TID for obesity management. Monitor renal function, lipid profile, HbA1c, CK, and potential drug interactions. Provide lifestyle counseling (diet, exercise, smoking cessation) and refer to a Diabetes Prevention Programme as per NICE CG181/PH46.
